Debrief

Thank you very much for participating in this study!

Many people learn about menopause from social media. We are replicating a published study to understand how the way menopause is portrayed affects how people feel, what they would do, and how they engage with the posts.

There were three versions of the posts: everyday experiences, distressing experiences, and experiences of positive change. Every participant is randomly shown only one version. We did not explain this earlier because knowing this could affect your answers.

Your responses are anonymous.

If you have questions, please contact andreaml@stanford.edu. Some posts could be upsetting or confusing. If you feel worried or if you have any questions about the menopause transition, you can talk to a doctor or another health professional.

Press the button to save your responses and finish.

trials.post_text: We need to stop labelling the menopause as a natural process where women endure symptoms... instead we should be calling it what it actually is: a long term hormone deficiency, which with the right support, treatments and lifestyle changes can be managed.
trials.stimulus:
Post 1 of 4

We need to stop labelling the menopause as a natural process where women endure symptoms... instead we should be calling it what it actually is: a long term hormone deficiency, which with the right support, treatments and lifestyle changes can be managed.

trials.post_text: Menopause symptoms should not be brushed aside as simply getting older. Falling hormone levels can disrupt sleep and daily life, and women need their difficulties to be taken seriously and their options for support discussed.
trials.stimulus:
Post 2 of 4

Menopause symptoms should not be brushed aside as simply getting older. Falling hormone levels can disrupt sleep and daily life, and women need their difficulties to be taken seriously and their options for support discussed.

trials.post_text: We need more honest conversations about the burden of menopause. Hot flushes, disturbed sleep and other symptoms can make everyday routines difficult, and women should not be left to struggle without information and appropriate care.

trials.post_text: Calling menopause a normal stage of life does not capture how challenging its symptoms can be. Hormonal changes can affect women's wellbeing, and those experiencing difficulties deserve support and a discussion of ways to manage them.

Debrief

Thank you very much for participating in this study!

Many people learn about menopause from social media. We are replicating a published study to understand how the way menopause is portrayed affects how people feel, what they would do, and how they engage with the posts.

There were three versions of the posts: everyday experiences, distressing experiences, and experiences of positive change. Every participant is randomly shown only one version. We did not explain this earlier because knowing this could affect your answers.

Your responses are anonymous.

If you have questions, please contact andreaml@stanford.edu. Some posts could be upsetting or confusing. If you feel worried or if you have any questions about the menopause transition, you can talk to a doctor or another health professional.

Please do not share details of the study with others who might participate.
